explain: A delegated task has its own lifecycle and artifact result rather than being just a synchronous remote function return. These are conceptual records, not literal A2A wire messages.
steps: Give accepted work a task identity and initial state. || Attach a produced artifact and terminal state after the work finishes.
name: remote-task

explain: Remote delegation carries only the necessary resource scope and audience. A remote agent cannot inherit authority merely from receiving task text.
steps: Define a constrained delegation record. || Reject a remote request for a resource outside that record.
name: delegated-scope

explain: Remote artifacts are untrusted content with type, size, and provenance checks. A successful remote status does not make embedded instructions executable.
steps: Validate the artifact envelope and maximum size. || Keep instruction-like text as data rather than dispatching it as a local command.
name: remote-artifact

explain: Delegation earns its extra network and coordination cost only when a required capability or ownership boundary justifies it. A second model with the same inputs is not automatically a useful remote specialist.
steps: Record whether a remote-only capability is required. || Compare the proposed architecture against the simpler local service baseline.
name: delegation-benefit
